clue.text: Jury members still strangely protected by sheets of glass

indicators.note: the letters of still are kept within the glass sheets, as if shielded by them

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass in a window, so several are panes

indicators.note: still behaving strangely means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jurors are oddly kept behind glass screens, as in some high-security trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adverb about the jury, but it is the fodder 'strangely' rearranges; 'protected by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Panel members, like the people on a jury or quiz show, are called by this collective term.

clue.text: A translation generating disgust

parts.note: a version of a text in another language is a translation

explanation.surface: A rendering of a text so poor it disgusts the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong dislike or repugnance is the synonym here; both name a feeling of revulsion.

clue.text: Girl's letter in very old-fashioned English

definitions.meaning: The wife of Ron Glum in the old British radio comedy The Glums, a short form of Ethel
a runic-derived character used in Old English writing for the th sound

explanation.walkthrough: Eth is a pet form of Ethel, familiar from the BBC radio sketch The Glums; the old letter looks like a crossed d.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the same three letters: a short girl's name and an Old English letter for th.

clue.text: Determination half gone after upset for sad type?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
five of the ten letters of the synonym disappear, leaving only its first half

parts.note: resolution means firm determination

explanation.surface: Someone whose resolve has crumbled after a setback is left feeling miserable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half gone' trims RESOLUTION to RESOL, and 'upset' turns that up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeated person, a sad sack or born failure, is the cryptic picture of a gloomy type.

clue.text: Soldier holding the line briefly — a spanking fellow?

indicators.note: the soldier wraps round the short line, keeping it inside

parts.note: a sapper is a military engineer, a soldier of the Royal Engineers
L is the standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A trooper who keeps in line seems a fine, upstanding fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spanking' looks like praise for a fine fellow, but the question mark points to a literal smacker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who slaps is literally a spanker, the playful sense the question mark flags.

clue.text: Attendant in place protecting a show

indicators.note: the place surrounds the other pieces as a guard surrounds what it shields

parts.note: a site is a place or location
taken as written
to tell can mean to show or reveal, as in telling the difference

explanation.surface: A steward at a venue guards a performance taking place there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' is the container signal; 'show' in the sense of reveal, as in 'time will tell'.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or hanger-on who waits upon a powerful figure can be called a satellite.

clue.text: Associate showing steel maybe, but no love

indicators.note: the circle for love is taken away, leaving the metal word without it

parts.note: steel is an example of an alloy, a mix of metals
love is nil in tennis scoring, shown by the letter O

explanation.surface: A friend displays a steely nature but no affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks steel as an example, and 'but no love' drops the O from ALLOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner or confederate is a synonym; both name someone joined with you in a cause.

clue.text: A lass loudly misbehaving when requiem is to be said

definitions.text: when requiem is to be said

indicators.note: the girl and the adverb behave badly, so their letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A girl is noisy and naughty at a solemn funeral service.
explanation.walkthrough: The requiem is the hint: a day in the Christian calendar, 2 November, when prayers are said for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Commemoration of the Faithful Departed is the feast when masses for the dead are offered.

clue.text: Not a dicky bird flying up to get shelter in tree

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from the bottom, so the word for nothing is turned

parts.note: British slang for nothing at all, i.e. nil
a den is a lair or hideaway

explanation.surface: A bird that is no bird soars up to roost in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a dicky bird' is British slang meaning not a word, nothing, so NIL; 'flying up' turns it to LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime tree is also known by this name, common in European avenues.

clue.text: Some losing heart bathed -— surprisingly one was healed in its pool

definitions.text: one was healed in its pool

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement signals the letters are mixed up
the middle letters of the word go, keeping only its two ends

explanation.surface: Someone who lost courage while bathing was surprisingly cured in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' cuts SOME to SE; 'surprisingly' shuffles SE with BATHED.
explanation.definitionFit: In St John's Gospel a lame man was cured by Jesus beside this pool in Jerusalem.

clue.text: Aptitude for producing story books of a religious nature

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, the scriptural books

explanation.surface: Someone has a gift for writing pious stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural gift or flair is the same idea as a knack for something.

clue.text: Compound is more complicated

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A chemical substance turns out more intricate than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry this is a molecule with the same atoms as another but arranged differently.

clue.text: Chairman's getting drunk on huge liqueurs

indicators.note: a drunk staggers, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the word with its s counted as a letter
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size meaning huge

explanation.surface: The chairman gets tipsy on enormous cherry liqueurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting drunk' signals the anagram; the possessive s on Chairman's is needed as a letter here. OS (outsize) is a British clothing size label.
explanation.definitionFit: These are cherry-flavoured liqueurs from Dalmatia, named after the marasca cherry.

clue.text: Garment turned up — left behind by mistress?

indicators.note: the little word is turned round so it reads the other way

parts.note: a mistress is a lover

explanation.surface: An item of clothing surfaces, abandoned by someone's mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses the little word up; 'behind by' simply places left before the mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted top pulled on over the head is a jumper or sweater.

clue.text: Try to gain approval from officer in hearing — this one?

parts.note: to court someone is to seek their favour

indicators.note: what an officer is called sounds, when heard, like the military adjective

parts.note: a marshal is a high-ranking officer, as in field marshal

explanation.surface: Seeking to impress a senior officer at a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The trial is military, so 'this one?' points to the officer's own court; the hearing also nods to that tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a service member on trial before a military court is to court-martial them.

clue.text: Huge human tragedy, by Jove, in Irish county

indicators.note: the oath sits inside the county name

parts.note: Meath is a county in the east of Ireland
egad is an old exclamation of surprise, like by Jove

explanation.surface: An exclamation at some vast calamity in rural Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Meath is a county of Ireland, north of Dublin; 'in' puts the oath inside it. Megadeath means a million deaths, chiefly in nuclear-war jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: The death of a million people, as in a nuclear war, is the literal sense.

clue.text: British put off drinking sessions bringing in American consumers

indicators.note: the remaining word takes the short American inside it
the British letter is put off, removed from the drinking bouts

parts.note: a bender is a drinking spree

explanation.surface: Britain discourages binge drinking that draws in American customers.
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is British slang for a drinking binge; 'put off' removes British, and 'bringing in' houses the American.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who finally use a product, rather than make or sell it, are its ultimate consumers.

clue.text: Something worth watching — football team playing without practice

parts.note: a sight is something worth seeing
Reading FC is an English football club

explanation.surface: A football team performs a spectacle with no rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: READING is an English football club, from the Berkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians performing a score at first sight, unrehearsed, are doing this.

clue.text: One sampling drink outside front of pub —— supplied by me once?

indicators.note: the sampler wraps round the pub's first letter

parts.note: a taster tries food or drink

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drinker sampling wine stands outside a pub he once supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives P, and 'outside' puts TASTER round it. The definition: an old word for a barman, who supplied the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word for a barman who drew beer from casks names who supplied the drink.

clue.text: Academic workers about to reach the end of term

definitions.text: to reach the end of term

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a degree holder
TU is a trade union, an organisation of workers
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: University staff wait out the close of the academic term.
explanation.walkthrough: The term here is financial: an insurance policy or bond matures when it reaches its term.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond or policy comes due when its fixed period ends, the financial sense.

clue.text: Worked in kitchen after meal, getting exhausted

explanation.surface: Doing the dishes after dinner leaves someone worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: cleaning the dishes after eating, and someone spent and finished.

clue.text: Perfume offered by tramp going round Scottish town

indicators.note: the tramp surrounds the town name

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A vagrant touring Scotland offers scent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a seaside town in south-west Scotland; 'going round' is the container signal, the tramp around the town.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic lotion from bay leaves and rum is used as an aftershave or hair tonic.

clue.text: Lighter force

definitions.meaning: a flat boat that carries goods to and from ships
to push roughly, as in to shove one's way in

explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed boat, and to push clumsily one's way is the verb sense.

clue.text: Arthur's wife, always leaving to go to a foreign country

indicators.note: the word for always leaves, taken out of the queen's name

parts.note: Guinevere was the queen of King Arthur
ever means always
taken as written

explanation.surface: King Arthur's queen leaves for good to go abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes EVER out of GUINEVERE, leaving GUINE, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African state with Conakry as its capital.

clue.text: Menace making king worry subsequently taken out

indicators.note: the time adverb is opened out to take the other pieces in

parts.note: then means afterwards
R stands for rex, Latin for king
to eat, as in what's eating you, means to worry

explanation.surface: A threat drives a king to fret, then be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out' is the container signal here: subsequently is opened out to take king and worry inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace someone is to intimidate them, the verb synonym here.

clue.text: Overwhelming feeling makes man weep regularly

indicators.note: every other letter, taken at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Emotion overcomes a man so that he weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverential wonder mixed with dread is a feeling that overwhelms.

clue.text: American author leaves female versifier for another woman

indicators.note: the writer departs, removed from the poet word

parts.note: a poetess is a female poet
Edgar Allan Poe, American writer of tales

explanation.surface: An American author leaves his female poet for another lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes POE out of POETESS; the answer is a girl's name, as in Hardy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as in Hardy's heroine, so a woman.

clue.text: Strong, healthy-sounding insects start to torment wild animal

indicators.note: the robust word is heard aloud, giving a near match in sound

parts.note: hearty means strong and healthy
bees are insects

indicators.note: the start of the word means its first letter

explanation.surface: Robust stinging insects begin to torment a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' is the homophone signal on the strong, healthy word; 'start to' takes the first letter of torment.
explanation.definitionFit: A large African antelope with curved horns is meant.
